findings.before: Both legacy and current resumable signup cleanup delete the incoming request. B finishes signup with no request; A must resend.
findings.intended: B sees the pending request and can accept it.

findings.before: normalizeGroup removes the other Alex solely by name; normalizeExpenses rewrites payer/splits to self. Dirty data is sent back to the backend. Mixed settlement states can also collapse.
findings.intended: Keep both UUIDs, original payer, and settlement amounts.

findings.before: Amounts are summed and settlement flags ANDed: the result is $25 unpaid. Backend and iOS use this aggregation.
findings.intended: Keep $15 outstanding and $10 settled.

findings.before: users.updateLinkedMemberId accepts that placeholder without owner/invite approval. A previously inaccessible private group and its expenses become readable. New accounts already receive random canonical IDs and cannot use this path.
findings.intended: Assign its own canonical identity; claiming someone else’s history requires consent-bound linking.

findings.before: The alias installs, but V2 group and expense visibility remain empty for mixed-owner or C-owned history. Legacy alias-aware queries can see the group. Current iOS uses V2.
findings.intended: B gains the relevant group/expense history after successful consent.

findings.before: The saved shares are $10 and −$5, totaling $5. Backend also accepts NaN totals and Infinity shares from malformed clients.
findings.intended: Reject or rebalance the adjustment so valid shares conserve the expense total.

findings.before: Currency changes the form’s presentation, but Expense, DTO and schema store no currency and no conversion occurs. Detail views label 100 with the viewer’s locale, e.g. $100.
findings.intended: Preserve denomination and value; balances must use an explicit currency contract.

findings.before: reconcileAfterNetworkRecovery invokes reconciliation without a context; stale-result checks are conditional. A’s remote friends can be merged with B’s current list.
findings.intended: Discard every completion from A.

findings.before: The real adapter ignores accountEmail and sends separately awaited upserts without per-write session/cancellation checks. Later rows may execute as B. Mocks partition by accountEmail and hide this risk.
findings.intended: Stop or reject A’s remaining writes.

findings.before: Name-keyed mapping collapses two friends into one and creates duplicate member IDs within a group. This also occurs with createNew.
findings.intended: Preserve each source identity unless the user explicitly merges it.

findings.before: Export omits contextKind. iOS import skips an expense without a mapped group; backend import also requires a group reference. One exported expense becomes zero imported. Notes are omitted for ordinary expenses too.
findings.intended: Restore context, participants, splits, settlement and notes.

findings.before: Exporter quotes it, but importer splits physical lines before CSV parsing; the expense fragments are silently skipped.
findings.intended: Round-trip the quoted multiline field.

findings.before: Importer appends every non-self group member to local friends with confirmed status. Production bulk import sends only explicit friend rows, causing local/server disagreement; the alternate CI path syncs the promoted list.
findings.intended: Keep the person in group history only.

findings.before: Client generates a new UUID; backend rejects another active token for the friend. Existing list/revoke APIs have no UI callers. The default active lifetime is 30 days.
findings.intended: Reuse the active invite or deliberately revoke and replace it.

findings.before: Decline changes accepted to declined; cancel deletes the accepted request. New marked links remain linked with inconsistent history; legacy links depending on historical evidence become visibly unlinked.
findings.intended: Reject terminal-state actions and preserve acceptance evidence.

findings.before: More than 64 relevant expenses reject. A fixed 80-lookups-per-ID estimate rejects 13 priced IDs at 1,040 > 1,024 even without aliases. Retrying cannot reduce history; no continuation exists.
findings.intended: Complete through safe bounded continuation.

findings.before: Clear-all removes derived visibility but not a durable exclusion. Later reconciliation recreates B’s visibility and the old expense reappears.
findings.intended: B remains detached while A’s history is preserved.

findings.before: Backend returns success:false for ghost/unlinked state. iOS discards the result, retains its deletion tombstone and hides a server row that still exists until reset.
findings.intended: Delete current server state or report failure and restore local state.

findings.before: Cleanup collects all owned expenses before targeting the person and rejects beyond 512. No resumable user path exists.
findings.intended: Complete friend deletion safely.

findings.before: Backend only looks up the supplied UUID and inserts a second container. Distinct expense IDs remain distinct; this alone does not double-count debt in the friend balance.
findings.intended: Reuse one identity-equivalent server ledger.

findings.before: Both payload classes persist; unrelated registered C receives visibility to the fabricated new expense. New-direct/grouped-individual paths have stronger matching-set checks than these paths.
findings.intended: Payer, splits and participant records must agree with the authorized identity set.

findings.before: C can read the new expense through the authenticated expense list even though B is unlinked. This shares/injects creator data into C’s account.
findings.intended: Derive registered recipients only from trusted member/link provenance.

findings.before: Email flow appends before sync and keeps the row after failure. Group-person detail uses addImportedFriend and immediately emits success. Normal Add Friend correctly awaits persistence.
findings.intended: Confirm and show success only after remote friend persistence.

findings.before: knownGroupParticipants first collapses UUIDs by name, so manualFriendCandidate sees an apparently unique person and reuses an arbitrary historical UUID.
findings.intended: Preserve ambiguity and require selection, or create a distinct identity.

findings.before: AppConfig has one pk_test_ key for all configurations; backend trusts the corresponding accounts.dev issuer. Clerk documents a 100-user development cap and says development instances are unsuitable for production.
findings.intended: Use coordinated production authentication and backend configuration.

findings.before: The confirmed row becomes request_sent while linked flags remain true. Current direct-expense eligibility survives. No active UI caller was found.
findings.intended: Keep confirmed status and return an idempotent result.

findings.before: B has the old manual A plus new linked canonical A. Email acceptance has no merge selection; Settings merge allows only two unlinked friends, so that UI cannot repair this pair afterward. Crossed requests or invite claim with selection behave differently.
findings.intended: Offer an explicit choice to merge B’s existing A record into linked A, preserving history. Do not guess from a name.

findings.before: B can still create because A’s persisted is_current_user flag bypasses A’s friendship check. Conversely, A’s notes-only update is rejected after A removes friendship.
findings.intended: Require confirmed friendship for new exposure; allow authorized owner edits to unchanged historical participants.

findings.before: Production stores three repeating Double fractions, displayed as $3.33 each. Existing rounding tests call a separate test-only helper that allocates cents correctly.
findings.intended: Allocate minor units deterministically, e.g. $3.34/$3.33/$3.33.
